children: Analog Devices
ADI shares have lost 5.6% in the past month compared with the Zacks Semiconductor - Analog and Mixed industry’s decline of 6.1%.
ADI One Month Performance Chart
ADI is trading at a forward price-to-sales multiple of 9.76X, much above the industry’s 7.74x. This premium valuation is further supported by the Zacks Value Score of D.
ADI Forward 12-Month (P/S) Performance Chart

Given the dynamics, investors are wondering if it is the right time to invest in ADI stock. Let’s delve deeper into the fundamentals and financials to know if it is the right time to buy, sell or retain ADI stock.
ADI Benefits From Industrial and Data Center Strength

ADI’s data center and power businesses are emerging as major growth drivers as AI infrastructure requires significantly higher power density, efficiency and monitoring capabilities. The company is benefiting from the shift toward 800V DC power distribution, driving increasing demand for 800V-to-intermediate power conversion technologies. ADI’s acquisition of Empower Semiconductor further strengthens its vertical power capabilities by enabling power delivery closer to the processor package.

Optical connectivity represents another important growth opportunity as AI data centers transition toward higher-speed architectures. ADI supplies timing, power management, data conversion, monitoring and control technologies for optical systems as customers move from 800 gigabits to 3.2 terabits per second. The company expects optical circuit switching revenues to approximately double in fiscal 2026, with similar growth targeted for fiscal 2027.

Co-packaged optics is also expanding ADI’s opportunity as rising thermal and serviceability complexity increases the need for precision control technologies. Analog Devices’ Industrial segment accounted for 49% of fiscal third-quarter 2026 revenues, rising 53% year over year and 10% sequentially to $1.97 billion. With continued investment, ADI is benefiting from higher revenues, improved utilization, favorable product mix and pricing actions.

ADI’s third-quarter adjusted gross margin increased 330 basis points year over year to 72.5%, while adjusted operating margin expanded 780 basis points to 50.0%. Adjusted operating expenses were $906.8 million, or 22.5% of revenue, compared with 27.1% a year earlier. Management expects further margin improvement in the fourth quarter, supported by favorable mix, higher fixed-cost absorption and pricing actions.
ADI Sustains Margins Despite Competitive Pressure

Competition in the high-performance analog semiconductor market remains intense, with Texas Instruments identified as a key rival given its manufacturing scale. ADI retains leadership in converters, although competitors continue to compete across multiple analog categories. ADI competes with
Texas Instruments
TXN,
STMicroelectronics
STM and
NXP Semiconductors
NXPI.

Texas Instruments competes across analog, digital and mixed-signal solutions, including precision sensing and power-management products for consumer electronics. NXP is a major provider of analog and mixed-signal semiconductor solutions for mobile, connectivity and consumer applications, including front-end, power-management and mixed-signal products, particularly in the mobile and IoT markets.

Texas Instruments also targets the automotive market through analog sensors, power ICs, in-vehicle networking, signal-chain products, and driver-assistance electronics. STMicroelectronics competes with ADI through products, including MEMS and inertial sensors, analog front ends, interface ICs and microcontrollers. Competition from these major semiconductor players has prompted ADI to increase research and development and sales and marketing investments at double-digit rates. Strong revenue growth has helped the company maintain its margins.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2026 earnings is pegged at $12.96 per share, implying 66.4% year-over-year growth. The consensus estimate has also moved higher over the past 30 days.
Conclusion: Buy ADI Stock Now

Analog Devices is benefiting from a broad-based recovery as Industrial demand improves and AI-related data center activity expands across optical and power applications. Long-cycle exposure to automation, test, aerospace and defense, energy systems and vehicle electrification supports durable growth. Sticky design wins and a flexible hybrid manufacturing model help capture demand while keeping channel inventories lean.
